summary.note: This edition replaces the #459-#482 edition. It audits the eight pull requests merged after it that claim a port or audit a port: #484, #497, #530, #531, #535, #538, #544 and #547. Each squash commit was re-read diff by diff against github.com/tailscale/tailscale at v1.102.4. Every finding below was checked against both the Go and the Rust. Where a divergence is disclosed in the merged commit or rustdoc, the finding says so. No finding is fixed here; each is left as tracked work.

gate.detail: All four steps green on main at 83d9556, run with CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4, RUST_TEST_THREADS=4, TS_RS_EXPERIMENT=this_is_unstable_software and the stable 1.95.0 toolchain: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --all-targets` (42 test targets, 1263 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored), `cargo build --release --bins`. Two machine facts, neither about the tree: the default toolchain here is a nightly with no clippy component, so clippy has to run on 1.95.0 (what CI's stable runner uses); and the first test run under a long session TMPDIR failed tailnetd's cleanup_refuses_live_socket with `path must be shorter than SUN_LEN` (darwin's 104-byte sun_path). Rerun with a short TMPDIR, test and release build both passed.

auditedPrs.notes: Squash 84f399d. The message change is accurate: at the pinned commit Go registers --bird-socket only under buildfeatures.HasBird, refuses it only when HookNewBird is unset, and sets the hook on linux, darwin, freebsd and openbsd, so the diff's citation of an older ref (53a0d659) hides no drift. Two divergences remain, both disclosed in the diff: the flag is refused on every platform, and the first line keeps an error: prefix, a trailing full stop and build text in place of GOOS.

Squash 4dce9c2 (the PR was reviewed in two rounds; one row covers both). The projection is sound, and it matches Go on three points: SelfChange has no mask bit of its own, it goes to every watcher, and it is set on the initial frame only under NotifyInitialNetMap. But self_change is tied to the engine's net_map peer tick rather than to a full netmap. So no frame is sent when only this node changed, a frame is sent on delta-only map responses where Go sends none, the self node is read after the tick instead of from the announced netmap, and the payload is a 5-field subset that always travels with the full peer list.

Squash a787db8. The core is right: set and check-prefs both judge the merged pref (Go's ApplyEdits then checkPrefsLocked), and check-prefs now reports auto-update before routes. Four divergences remain. set stops at the first error and checks routes before auto-update. A config-file opt-in fails the config load where Go accepts it. The refusal text is not Go's. And up never checks the auto-update pref.

Squash a38687b. The four CheckTag reasons, the `tag: %q: %s` frame, the clause order, the bare-name completion (Go also prepends tag: when there is no colon), quoting the completed value and stopping at the first offender all match. One divergence: Rust's {:?} is not Go's %q for control bytes, so the commit's claim that the message is identical for every string CheckTag can reach does not hold.

Squash a8b5fbf. The four refusals it retags match Go's strings exactly. Their framing does too: Go's main prints cli.Run's error bare and exits 1, and RunWithContext rewrites only help and access-denied errors. The serve/funnel error surface around them still diverges. The two --service refusals still print through the `Caused by` chain, and a new test pins that output. Every daemon-stage serve/funnel error keeps the same wrapper. The integration tests pin a check order that puts the PROXY checks ahead of Go's daemon-side funnel check. And the mount-point message quotes the path with {:?} rather than %q.

Squash c872cca. The main fix matches Go: every interrupted run now exits 0, and the pref is put back only under Go's `!webArgs.cgi && startedManagementClient` guard. One divergence remains, and the new doc comment says the opposite of what the code does: the interrupt handler is armed after the pref step, where Go arms signal.NotifyContext as runWeb's first statement. The PR's disclosed claim that the listener keeps accepting during teardown is overstated, because tokio::select! drops the serve future before the branch body runs, which matches Go's Shutdown-then-setRunWebClient order.

Squash 3977ad9 (reviewed and audited as one PR). reload_and_publish faithfully ports the tail of reloadNow: swap and compare under a lock, then notify only when the policy changed. It is now the only sender, and both the per-session feed and the backend reconcile hang off it, as Go's two change callbacks do. There are two disclosed divergences, both unobservable today. The first load publishes a tick where Go's old != nil guard sends none, and the comparison runs over rendered rows, where AuthKey is redacted, instead of over the raw items.

Squash ddd2fb8, a docs-only PR that rewrote this file for #459 through #482. Every Go path it cites exists at the pinned commit, and its totals match its rows. Spot checks confirmed the #476 verifyFunnelEnabled finding, the #469 and #466 --assert findings, the #472 log-prefix and ReadOnlyServerMode findings, the #459 syspolicy-list finding, and the faithful #481 and #463 rows. Three findings are wrong or stale. The #459 log-line finding says Go's line has no Start: prefix, and it does. The #466 finding states the wrong Go output for a stopped node. The #482 tag-wording finding was already fixed on main when the audit merged.

findings.title: No self_change frame is sent when only this node changed
findings.detail: Go builds Notify.SelfChange in setControlClientStatusLocked from st.NetMap.SelfNode on every full netmap, and sends it to every watcher (on non-Windows with no NetMap attached). The merged stream_notify (src/server.rs) fetches the self node only when the engine emits net_map, and the engine emits that only from peer_rx.changed(). So a key-expiry extension, a MagicDNS rename or new self addresses, which are the events the field exists to report, produce no frame at all when only this node changed. The rustdoc on the field discloses it and it is filed as an engine ask, which makes the real fix engine-side.

findings.title: The two --service refusals print through a `funnel via <socket>` / Caused by chain, not as Go's single line
findings.detail: Go returns errors.New("Error: --service flag is not supported with funnel") and its background-mode twin, and main prints each one bare on a single line. The merged Rust literals carry no prefix, and main wraps every serve/funnel result in .with_context("serve via|funnel via <socket>") (src/bin/tnet.rs). The actual stderr is therefore `Error: funnel via <sock>`, a blank line, `Caused by:` and the sentence indented. The new test the_two_service_refusals_are_left_as_they_were (tests/serve_refusal_stderr_framing.rs) asserts that divergent output. This is the other half of the rule the PR states: Go spells the prefix itself for these two, and the PR only stopped them doubling instead of reproducing them.

findings.title: --bird-socket is refused on every platform, where Go accepts it on linux, darwin, freebsd and openbsd
findings.detail: Go fatals only when `buildfeatures.HasBird && birdSocketPath != "" && !wgengine.HookNewBird.IsSet()`; feature/condregister/maybe_bird.go sets the hook for `!ts_omit_bird && (linux || darwin || freebsd || openbsd)`, so a default build on those four accepts the flag and hands the path to the engine config as BIRDSocket. The merged can_use_bird() (src/bin/tailnetd.rs) always returns Err, so tailnetd refuses the flag on every platform. The diff discloses this and puts it down to the engine exposing no BIRD hook, which makes the real fix engine-side; it is still a loss of function for a BIRD user on Linux.

findings.title: The --bird-socket refusal keeps an error: prefix, a full stop and build text where Go prints one bare GOOS line
findings.detail: Go runs log.SetFlags(0) and log.Fatalf("--bird-socket is not supported on %s", runtime.GOOS), so stderr is exactly `--bird-socket is not supported on linux` and exit 1. The merged first line is `error: --bird-socket is not supported on this platform or in this build of tailnetd.`, followed by advice paragraphs. The diff moved the rejected path off line 1, which was its stated goal, and discloses the rest, but a match anchored to the start of the line or on Go's whole line still fails.

findings.title: self_change is sent on delta-only map responses, where Go sends none
findings.detail: In Go, a map response the client can apply incrementally (online/last-seen changes, peer patches) goes through tryHandleIncrementally and UpdateNetmapDelta and returns before UpdateFullNetmap; the Notify that UpdateNetmapDelta produces carries no SelfChange. The pinned engine re-publishes its peer watch on liveness-only and patch-only responses, and each of those becomes a net_map frame that the merged code decorates with self_change. Watchers therefore get "self changed" frames on peer churn. The rustdoc redefines the field as "the netmap moved", which is not Go's meaning. This is not disclosed.

findings.title: The self node is read after the tick rather than taken from the netmap being announced
findings.detail: Go takes SelfNode from the same netmap it announces, under b.mu, both on updates and in the initial notify. The merged code calls dev.self_node() separately after the peer tick arrives, bounded by the 500 ms STATUS_QUERY_TIMEOUT (src/ipn/mod.rs). The self it attaches can therefore come from a different netmap than the peers in the same frame. On a timeout or error the frame goes out with no self node even though the netmap had a valid one; Go leaves the field nil only when SelfNode is invalid.

findings.title: SelfReport is a 5-field subset of Go's tailcfg.Node and always rides with the full peer list
findings.detail: Go's Notify.SelfChange (ipn/backend.go) is a whole *tailcfg.Node: CapMap, Tags, User, the full Addresses list, and the FQDN Name with its trailing dot. The merged SelfReport (src/localapi.rs) carries stable_id, a display name, ipv4, ipv6 and key_expiry. Omitting a never-expiring key_expiry does match Go's omitzero. Every self frame also carries the full net_map, whereas Go's runtime SelfChange frames on non-Windows carry none. The subset is disclosed as a decision.

findings.title: set stops at the first error and checks advertise-routes before auto-update
findings.detail: Go's editPrefsLocked calls checkPrefsLocked(p1). That function collects every violation with errors.Join in a fixed order: SSH, exit node, funnel, then checkAutoUpdatePrefsLocked, then checkAdvertiseRoutes. The merged begin_set_gated (src/ipn/mod.rs) runs validate_advertise_routes(...)? before the auto-update check and returns on the first error. So a set that violates both rules reports only the route error, in the opposite order to Go's. The diff reordered only check_prefs, and the comment beside the set path says it follows check_prefs's order, which holds only for the SSH-then-auto-update pair.

findings.title: A config-file opt-in to AutoUpdate.Apply fails the config load, where Go accepts it
findings.detail: Go's initPrefsFromConfig and setConfigLocked only run ToPrefs, ApplyEdits and SetPrefs/setPrefsLocked. They never call checkPrefsLocked, so a Go daemon boots with the opt-in and advertises AllowsUpdate. The merged Config::apply_to_prefs (src/conffile.rs) refuses the whole config with `config: AutoUpdate.Apply: ...`. The diff presents this as a new rule meant to stop a dishonest advertisement; that is a deliberate policy choice, but it is a behaviour Go does not have.

findings.title: The auto-update refusal text is not Go's sentence
findings.detail: Go's checkAutoUpdatePrefsLocked returns exactly `Auto-updates are not supported on this platform.`. It also has a build-gate message, `Auto-update support is disabled in this build`, which has no counterpart here. The merged src/ipn/selfupdate.rs keeps Go's sentence only as the prefix of the no-release-artifact branch and appends an explanation and a caller-chosen remedy. The Homebrew branch reads `Auto-updates are not supported on this installation: ...`, where Go says "on this platform" because CanAutoUpdate is simply false. The diff changed how this refusal text ends without bringing it back to Go's wording.

findings.title: up never checks the auto-update pref, so a stored opt-in does not fail tailscale up as it does in Go
findings.detail: On a running node, Go's tailscale up goes through EditPrefs (cmd/tailscale/cli/up.go), and Start with UpdatePrefs also runs checkPrefsLocked, so a persisted opt-in on a host that cannot update fails up too. The merged begin_up (src/ipn/mod.rs) never calls check_auto_update_pref; its only callers are the set path, check_prefs and the config loader. The diff's title says "every ingress", and up is an ingress it leaves unchecked (disclosed as an open question).

findings.title: Tag refusals quote with Rust {:?}, which differs from Go's %q for control characters
findings.detail: Go formats the refusal as fmt.Errorf("tag: %q: %s", tag, err), and strconv.Quote writes control bytes as \x01 or \x7f. The merged complete_and_validate_advertise_tags (src/ipn/mod.rs) uses {t:?}, which writes \u{1} or \u{7f}. So --advertise-tags with a control byte in the name (e.g. tag:a followed by 0x01) gets a different quoted value than tailscale up prints. The commit says the two quote identically for every ASCII input CheckTag can reach, and that claim is false for these bytes.

findings.title: Daemon-stage serve/funnel errors still print as `Error: ... via <socket>` plus Caused by
findings.detail: Everything else runServeCombined returns, Go prints bare: `error getting serve config: %w`, `getting client status: %w`, `service hosts must be tagged nodes`, `missing SessionID`. So does serve reset/status's LocalAPI error (cmd/tailscale/cli/serve_legacy.go). In Rust all of these pass through the same main-level with_context wrapper and anyhow's Termination rendering, so they gain an `Error: serve via <socket>` header and a Caused by block that Go never prints.

findings.title: The new integration tests pin a check order in which PROXY refusals come before Go's funnel check
findings.detail: For funnel, Go calls verifyFunnelEnabled(ctx, 443) (cmd/tailscale/cli/funnel.go), which talks to the daemon, before cleanURLPath and the PROXY-protocol checks. The tun refusal also comes after GetServeConfig and the status calls. Rust decides all four retagged refusals before it touches the socket, and tests/serve_refusal_stderr_framing.rs asserts that `tnet funnel --proxy-protocol=1 3000` prints the PROXY refusal with no daemon, a case where Go would first fail at the daemon or at the funnel-capability step. This overlaps the earlier missing-verifyFunnelEnabled finding, but this PR adds tests that lock in the check order.

findings.title: The mount-point refusal quotes the path with {:?}, not Go's %q
findings.detail: Go's cleanURLPath error is fmt.Errorf("failed to clean the mount point: %w", ...) wrapping a message that quotes the path with %q. The merged mount-point refusal formats it with {with_slash:?} (src/bin/tnet.rs), so a control byte such as ESC in --set-path renders as \u{1b} where Go writes \x1b. The PR claims this sentence is now Go's exactly, and that is true only for printable paths. The quoting code predates the PR.

findings.title: The web interrupt handler is armed after the pref step, not as runWeb's first statement
findings.detail: Go's runWeb begins with signal.NotifyContext(ctx, os.Interrupt), before StatusWithoutPeers, GetPrefs and setRunWebClient(ctx, true). A SIGINT during that step either fails setRunWebClient with `starting web client in tailscaled: context canceled`, or is seen by the goroutine, which turns the pref back off and exits 0. The merged run_web (src/bin/tnet.rs) awaits start_tailscaled_web_client(socket) first, which is three LocalAPI round trips, and only then polls web_interrupt() inside serve_until_interrupt. tokio::signal::ctrl_c() installs its handler on first poll, so the handler is armed after the pref step and a SIGINT inside that window still takes the default disposition: exit 130, and RunWebClient left on if the set had already landed. The new doc on web_interrupt says it is armed "as its first statement - before the pref step", which the code does not do.

findings.title: Registering the first policy source publishes a change on the first load, which Go suppresses
findings.detail: Go's reloadNow invokes the change callbacks only under `if old != nil && !old.EqualItems(new)`, so the first resolution of a scope from newPolicy notifies nobody. The merged LAST_PUBLISHED (src/ipn/syspolicy.rs) starts as an empty snapshot, so the first load_json_policy_file that sets any key publishes a tick on this first load. The divergence is disclosed and reasoned. It cannot be observed because the file loads before the LocalAPI serves.

findings.title: The change test compares rendered rows with AuthKey redacted, where Go hashes raw items
findings.detail: Go's Snapshot.EqualItems compares the length and then a deephash of the raw RawItem map, and that map includes the real AuthKey value. The merged reload_and_publish compares Vec<PolicySetting> rows, where AuthKey is rendered as <redacted>, so a change that only rotates the AuthKey value would not notify here but would notify in Go. This is disclosed, and it cannot happen today because only one source is ever registered, and only once.

findings.title: The #459 log-line finding says Go's skip line has no Start: prefix; Go's does
findings.detail: Go's startLocked logs through logf := logger.WithPrefix(b.logf, "Start: "), so both the `not setting opts.AuthKey from syspolicy` line and the `setting opts.AuthKey by syspolicy, len=%v` line carry the Start: prefix. The committed finding against #459 says upstream has no `Start: ` prefix. The rest of that finding (the len=%v text and the flattened branch) is accurate.

findings.title: The #466 finding gives the wrong Go output for `tailscale ip` on a stopped node
findings.detail: The committed finding says `tailscale ip` on a node brought down with `down` prints `no current Tailscale IPs; state: Stopped`. In Go, Status's TailscaleIPs are taken from the netmap. Entering Stopped does not clear the netmap; only resetForProfileChangeLocked does. So a stopped node that still holds a netmap prints its addresses. The Rust divergence the finding reports (`error: node is not up`) is real, but the Go behaviour it is measured against is misstated.

findings.title: The #482 tag-wording finding describes code that was already fixed on main when the audit merged
findings.detail: The finding against #482 says tag refusals are reworded (`invalid tag ...: tags must be of the form ...`). That was true of #482's own code. But #538 (a38687b, an ancestor of ddd2fb8) had already switched src/ipn/mod.rs to Go's `tag: %q: %s` frame and the four CheckTag sentences verbatim. The audit narrowed its #479 finding for a later fix on main but not this one, so a reader following this row would chase a divergence that was already fixed.
